missionPremise: The third-party review's finding (_inbox/2026-09-10_ctx_third_party_review.md section 2): verify-walk.mjs's gradeParcelResponse grades ~180 sampled parcels per county by one HTTP read each, short-circuits on a non-ok response (478-480) or an earned retirement (490-522), and its content check (gradeTier1Content) validates a hand-grown required-leaf list against only a four-state contract. scripts/ctx-prov/provenance-population.mjs re-expressed one walk predicate as SQL over the whole store and found 18,037 rows a sampled walk had surfaced as a single parcel. CTX-B3 generalises that precedent: a file-based, self-tested script that reads every place_layer_snapshots tier-1 row per county and classifies the leaves the bake owns, the four dollar fields, owner name, and the structural tier, reporting counts per (county, leaf, state), refusing on any unrecognised state or sentinel, with an instrument falsifier tested against the real walk.
completionPredicate: A read-only script exists that reads every place_layer_snapshots tier-1 row per county (not a sample), classifies each dimension the dispatch named, reports per-(county,leaf,state) counts naming the store, refuses (does not silently pass) every sentinel class the review named that is reproducible in this table's schema, is self-tested with the three required fixtures each observed failing before passing, has its own falsifier tested against the real walk's gradeTier1Content on real rows (not merely asserted equivalent by shared code), does not modify the walk/BP-CONTENT-01/the permitted state set/the sampler, was run for real against staging for all six counties, and is merged with green CI (literal conclusion string 'success').
scopeBasis: Exactly what the dispatch named: read-only census of place_layer_snapshots tier-1 rows, leaf list from BAKE_OWNED_REQUIRED_LEAF_PATHS at the pin, the four dollar fields, owner name, structural tier, self-test plus falsifier, no modification of the walk/BP-CONTENT-01/permitted state set/sampler, no deploy/build/job/bake/publish/walk. Deliberately excluded: parcel_record_cell (a different table with a different place_key shape, named explicitly in the dispatch's own trap section and confirmed to be where two of the review's named sentinel examples actually live -- see leaf_list_corrections); any change to legacy-design-tools, hauska-engine, or hauska-map; production (this lane ran staging only -- the dispatch says 'either target', and staging is the lower-blast-radius choice for a first full-store run of a brand-new instrument; production is a one-flag rerun the integration seat or a follow-up can take, named in whatsRemainsOpen).

LESSON: A shared, non-worktree checkout of a dependency repo (here, P:/legacy-design-tools) is unsafe for ANY script that reads files from its WORKING TREE (as opposed to `git show <sha>:<path>`, which reads the object database and is safe regardless of what is checked out) when other concurrent lanes may check that same path out to other commits mid-session. The safe pattern, already established by CTX-WALKRULE and reused here: a throwaway scratch clone under the session's own scratchpad, pinned via `git fetch --depth 1 origin <exact-sha>`, never the shared path.

A static, string-literal-only data export (BAKE_OWNED_REQUIRED_LEAF_PATHS: readonly string[]) does not need the full esbuild-bundle-and-execute machinery a REAL predicate function needs (record-retirement.mjs's loadIsEarnedRecordRetirement). Reading it as text from `git show <pin>:<path>` with a narrow regex, cross-validated against the source file's OWN test assertion of the identical literal, is simpler, has no runtime dependency surface (no DATABASE_URL shim, no pnpm install), and is exactly as rigorous for data as the bundling approach is for behavior.

verify-walk.mjs's tier1PayloadOf prefers body.facets when present -- correct for an HTTP response body (a route nests the payload under .facets), and SILENTLY WRONG if applied to a place_layer_snapshots row directly, because that row carries its own small, unrelated facets:{base:{...}} sub-object. Any future script reading gradeTier1Content/classifyRequiredLeaf against a raw DB row must wrap as {payload: row.payload_json} first. This cost real time to find and would have produced a systematically-wrong (but consistent-looking) census if it had not been caught before the full scan.
